newsitem.title: POLAND: GM starts Polish car plant construction.
newsitem.headline: GM starts Polish car plant construction.

text.p: General Motors on Wednesday launched the construction of a 470 million mark ($308.2 million) automotive plant in Poland to assemble 72,000 passenger cars annually from 1998.

"This venture goes beyond a simple investment. It is a long-term commitment to the future of the region and Poland," said David Herman, president of GM's German subsidiary Adam Opel AG, which will run the plant.

The ground-breaking ceremony, in the Silesian southern city of Gliwice, was attended by German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski, who said the investment was further proof of the fast-growing Polish economy's progress in integration with Western Europe.
"It is symbolic that here in Gliwice, where World War Two started, we open a new chapter in the relations between Poland and Germany," Kinkel told the ceremony.
Kinkel said he was confident German investors, who have brought $1.3 billion to Poland, would soon catch up with those from the United States, who have contributed $2.4 billion.
Since 1990, the year after the fall of communism, foreign investment has totalled $10.2 billion.

The Gliwice factory, employing 2,000 people in an area threatened by massive lay-offs from an ailing mining industry, will resemble Opel's state-of-the-art assembly plant in the German city of Eisenach.
It will assemble a low-cost family car based on the Opel/Vauxhall Astra model.

The plant will include metal stamping, welding, paint and final assembly units, which could be expanded after additional investment. After several years about 60 percent of parts used for assembly will come from Poland.
GM decided to launch a green-field project in Poland after it lost a race with South Korea's Daewoo Corp last year to take over the state-owned FSO car plant.

As investment incentives the government has offered the plant, in a special economic zone, a 10-year exemption from the country's 40-percent corporate tax and a customs duty break on car parts import.
GM will continue to assemble Astra models in a existing small joint-venture in Warsaw, in which a minority stake belonged to FSO but which was taken over by the treasury after the Daewoo purchase.

Daewoo, which wants to invest about $1.5 billion in its two Polish plants to produce some 300,000 units annually, is one of several car firms lured by Poland's booming auto market strategic location between Russia and the European Union. @

New car sales in Poland jumped nearly 36 percent to 260,000 in the first eight months of 1996 compared with the same period last year. Analysts say they should grow to more than 500,000 units annually in the year 2000.

Italy's Fiat Spa, which bought the FSM small car factory in 1992, remains the biggest player in Poland's car industry with more than 40 percent of the market. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700 ($ = 1.525 German Marks)
